subject: FintechAI - cost/pricing qualification & latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Patel <chris@fintechai.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechAI discovery recap + next steps (tokens, budget, latency)

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for the call today, great to hear more about FintechAI's roadmap and how you're thinking about both UI experiments and higher-volume backend batch jobs. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size pricing/POC correctly: 

What we heard
- Primary product is customer-facing insights (low-latency UI flows) plus nightly batch scoring for model retraining.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ballpark asked for (you to confirm) ~50M tokens/month, with 6-10M tokens/day at peak.
- Latency SLO: UI p95 target ~400ms; background jobs can tolerate up to ~1.5s.
- Budget: you mentioned a target range but asked for unit economics; will you confirm target $/1M tokens?

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm expected monthly tokens (avg + peak) and a target budget per 1M tokens? (this helps us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated).
2) If procurement needs to be looped in, please share the contact + procurement timeline.
3) I attached our current pricing tiers and a quick sample mapping file for how tokens map to your events.

What I'm going to do
- Draft two options: Hosted (Standard vs Premium with streaming) and Dedicated reserved capacity with commit economics, and show estimated $/1M tokens at your volume.
- Call out trade-offs: lower unit cost with Dedicated + commit vs higher flexibility + instant scale on Hosted; streaming + smaller batch sizes reduce p95 but increase unit cost; batching increases throughput and lowers unit cost but can hurt p95.

Attaching: Redwood_pricing_tiers_Q2.pdf, sample_map_tokens.csv

Possible times for a quick follow-up next week to walk numbers: Monday or Tuesday AM PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Chris Patel <chris@fintechai.com>

Cc: procurement <procurement@fintechai.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechAI discovery recap + next steps (tokens, budget, latency)

Thanks Marissa, useful recap. A few clarifications: 

- Volumes: current estimate is indeed ~50M tokens/month average. Peak daily could be ~8M tokens on promo days. Over the next 6 months we expect 2x growth, but for quoting please assume 50M baseline.
- Budget: our finance lead gave a target band of $1,500 to $3,000 per 1M tokens depending on latency/SLA. Our sweet spot would be closer to $1,800/1M if latency can meet the UI SLO.
- Latency SLOs: UI p95 target 400ms. For non-UI/background batch jobs >1s acceptable. If you offer streaming / chunked responses for the UI we would prioritize lower p95 even at some uplift in unit cost.

Procurement is looped (procurement@fintechai.com), they typically need an initial quote + contract template. Timeline: procurement wants a PO in ~3 weeks if costs align.

Happy to do a 2-week POC if it helps prove unit economics and tail latencies.

-Chris
Head of Product | FintechAI
chris@fintechai.com

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechAI discovery recap + next steps (tokens, budget, latency)

Great, thanks for the clarity, Chris. I've also attached a draft quote and a short PoC plan.

Option A - Hosted (Standard)
- Unit economics (estimate at 50M/mo): ~ $2,200 per 1M tokens (note: illustrative; final depends on model choice and exact sequence lengths).
- Performance: p50 ~100ms, p95 ~350-450ms (depends on batch settings).
- Upside: immediate onboarding, no infra commit, simple billing.
- Downside: higher per-unit compared to commit, potential variability on tail latency during spikes.

Option B - Hosted (Premium) w/ streaming
- Unit economics: ~ $3,600 per 1M tokens.
- Performance: p95 ~120-200ms with streaming + smaller batch sizes.
- Upside: best UI experience, lower tail latency, simpler integration for chunked responses.
- Downside: higher unit cost; recommended if UI p95 is strict and worth the uplift.

Option C - Dedicated Reserved Capacity (12mo commit)
- Effective unit cost at your volume: ~ $1,400-1,700 per 1M tokens (depending on commit level).
- Performance: p95 ~100-200ms typical with reserved GPU pools and tuned kernels.
- Upside: best cost at scale, predictable throughput, stronger isolation for compliance.
- Downside: commit required and longer lead time to provision if you need on-prem/network controls.

Operational levers (how to hit your $1,800/1M goal)
- Batching: increase batch size for non-UI to lower unit cost; for UI keep small batch/streaming.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts reduces tokens billed.
- Quantization/model choice: switching from fp16 to int8 variants can drop per-token runtime cost but must be validated on quality.
- SLO-driven routing: route UI requests to Premium/low-latency pool and background to Dedicated/cheaper pool; automatic fallback policy if capacity constrained.

Proposal
- Run a 2-week POC: we instrument real traffic (redacted), measure p50/p95, and produce a cost projection with three scenarios (baseline, 2x growth, peak day).
- Deliverables: latency report, per-route cost estimates, implementation playbook for SLO-driven routing and batch settings.
- Attachments: 20260621_Redwood_quote_FintechAI.pdf, PoC-plan.docx

Next steps
- Confirm: (1) POC start date (we can start as early as June 29), (2) procurement contact and contract cadence, (3) whether you want us to include Dedicated sizing in the initial quote.

If it helps I can put together a one-page cost vs latency matrix keyed to the exact model you plan to use.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Please send the quote and PoC plan and I'll route to procurement.

Thanks,
Chris
